outcome: No result found that changes the stated 1-factorization conjecture (that a k-regular graph on 2n vertices with k >= n (n odd) or k >= n-1 (n even) is 1-factorable) since 26 January 2024. The conjecture remains proved only for sufficiently large n (Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus & Treglown, 2016, arXiv:1401.4159 et seq.), a pre-window result. All post-window activity found concerns distinct, related conjectures (the perfect 1-factorisation conjecture of Kotzig, and the Overfull Conjecture), not this one.
summary: The 1-factorization conjecture as stated (a k-regular graph on 2n vertices is 1-factorable if k >= n for n odd, or k >= n-1 for n even) was proved only for sufficiently large n by Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Treglown in a four-part series (arXiv:1401.4159, .4164, .4178, .4183), all posted in January 2014 — well before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision, and already reflected in the pre-window Wikipedia text. I re-verified this is still the state of the art: the current Graph factorization Wikipedia article (fetched live, for context only) still describes the conjecture as proved only for 'sufficiently large n', with no update since 2016. I searched broadly for any 2024-2026 movement — full resolution, resolution for small n, or any bound improvement — and found none. The only post-window hits are: (1) 'The perfect 1-factorisation conjecture holds asymptotically' (Cheng & Sgueglia, arXiv:2607.09459, submitted 10 July 2026), which addresses Kotzig's conjecture — a genuinely different, stronger statement about decomposing the complete graph K_n specifically into n-1 perfect matchings that pairwise form Hamilton cycles, not about general k-regular graphs on 2n vertices meeting a degree threshold; this is a related problem under §3.1, not a case of the stated conjecture, since it changes the object (only K_n) and the requirement (Hamilton-cycle-pairing, not mere 1-factorability); and (2) 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture II' (arXiv:2607.02270), which is an unrelated edge-coloring conjecture (about overfull subgraphs forcing class-2 status) that does not cite or bear on the 1-factorization conjecture. I also checked for any multigraph-variant developments; the multigraph 1-factorization conjecture (Plantholt-Tipnis) was addressed asymptotically by Vaughan back in 2010 (arXiv:1010.5192), also pre-window and also a distinct variant (multigraphs with bounded multiplicity, not simple regular graphs). No AI system appears anywhere in this literature; all identified papers are conventional human-authored extremal/probabilistic graph theory arguments (absorption method, regularity method), with no mention of AI, machine learning, or automated proof assistance in any source I opened. I judge the search complete: I checked the current Wikipedia article, ran multiple targeted arXiv/web searches for the exact conjecture and its known variants, and opened every source that could plausibly bear on it.
competing_reading: None of substance. One could argue the Kotzig perfect 1-factorisation asymptotic result deserves mention as adjacent progress in the same research cluster, but by the letter of §3.1 it changes the stated question (restricting to K_n, and adding the Hamilton-cycle-pairing condition) rather than restricting it, so it is a related problem, not a case, and does not belong in `event`.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving the conjecture for all n (removing the 'sufficiently large' restriction), or proving/disproving it for any specific small n not yet covered, would count as progress or resolution. No such paper was found.
